1:# Brief — idea of the study (revision 12: P7 noise part as the analytic limit; operational P6/P7 definitions confirmed against `analysis` addendum 5)
12:2. **Bias is the unidentified part.** It is fixed by the response at the corners, which lie outside (or at the tail of) the observed exposure distribution. Two responses that agree on the observed support and differ at the corner generate the same data distribution and different GATE, so no function of the data alone can be consistent for the bias without a restriction on the response class; every restriction (the specification ladder, a curvature bound) is an assumption, and the disagreement among ladder specifications only detects bias that the ladder's specifications do *not* share. *Order of events:* P5(ii) was predicted to work and failed; this argument came afterwards, as an explanation of the failure, and it is tested by P6 and P7, not anticipated by the pre-registration. It explains, rather than excuses, the failed P5 (ii): the exact-theory predictor explains |bias| (R² 0.99) because it uses the true response; the data-computable ones sit below the constant. The corner is partly inside the support at small d (the threshold straddling at d=5) — identification is partial, which is why the bias depends on d by mechanism.
14:4. **Inference follows the same split:** the HC0 interval's undercoverage tracks |bias|/SD, not leverage; the variance-calibrated interval is right when bias is small and wrong when it is not. An interval that is honest about the unidentified part has to be indexed to an assumption (P6).

## main...origin/main
  - **Prior work for the form.** The interval is of the honest-confidence-interval type (Armstrong & Kolesár 2018, 2020: add the worst-case bias over a derivative-bounded class; the bound must be chosen a priori, not adapted to from the data, for centrosymmetric convex classes) with their rule-of-thumb M̂ (sup of the second derivative of a global polynomial fit) as the calibration; κ × the in-support magnitude is the relative-magnitudes logic of Rambachan & Roth 2023 (abstract only read). **Not claimed as new.** What the study adds is the application to the extrapolation functional of exposure regressions (the corner offsets c(p) and their degree dependence), the test against controls, and κ* (below).
  - **Interval.** τ̂ ± cv_α(κB/SE)·SE_HC0, with cv_α(t) the (1−α) quantile of |N(t,1)| (the fixed-length form; it is shorter than the linear sum z·SE + κB at the same worst-case coverage, which is therefore not run), α = 0.10, with B a data-computable bound on the extrapolation term for a stated class: **B₁** = the range of τ̂ across the pre-listed specification ladder (class: the truth is as curved as some ladder member); **B₂** = ½·M̂·c(p), c(p) = (1−p)² + p² (class: curvature beyond the support is no larger than κ times the curvature inside it). **M̂ fixed in advance:** the largest |∂²/∂f²| over the observed range of the treated-neighbour fraction (minimum to maximum, both own-treatment arms) of the global **cubic** polynomial in f fitted with z and z×f (the rule of thumb; no splines or knots, so it is defined at d = 5 where f has six values). κ grid fixed in advance: {0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64}; all κ are reported.
  - **κ\*** (the main quantity, replaces "coverage at some κ ≤ 2"): per mechanism × d (pooled over p, s, graph draws), the smallest κ in the grid with mean coverage ≥ 0.90, ∞ if none. It measures how much assumption each mechanism needs, **net of SE miscalibration**: HC0 undercovers without any bias (high leverage, small n), so κ\* is also computed on the **zero-bias null cells** (the mechanism-free null column s = 0, present in the original runs and required in the block) as κ\*₀, and reported both raw and as the excess κ\* − κ\*₀; on a subset (one graph per mechanism × d at p = 0.5) it is recomputed with the SE replaced by the Monte-Carlo SD of τ̂ (known in Tier G), and if κ\* barely moves the SE is not the issue. non-identification predicts that it varies over orders of magnitude and has no finite value for the unidentifiable cases. Also reported for B₁.
  - **Predictions (falsifiable).** (1) *Smooth mechanisms* (a), (b), (c), (e), (f) (and on the block (g), (h)): κ\* for B₂ is ≤ 2 for the median mechanism × d cell. **Frozen κ̂** = the smallest grid value at which the mean over the smooth mechanisms (equal weight per mechanism, then over cells) of coverage is ≥ 0.90 on the original cells, computed by `analysis` before the block is run and recorded; κ̂ is also computed leave-one-mechanism-out on the original cells (held-out mechanism's coverage at the κ chosen on the others). (2) *Threshold (d), outside the support, defined from the design:* the treated corner is outside the support when q(d, p, θ) = P(Bin(d,p)/d ≥ θ) < 0.05 with θ = 0.6 (e.g. d = 20, p = 0.25; d = 80, p = 0.25); for these cells κ\* is either ∞ (no value in the grid) or at least max(8 × the median κ\* of the smooth mechanisms, 4) (so a smooth median at the grid floor does not make the criterion trivial); (d) cells with q ≥ 0.05 are partly identified and reported separately. If κ\* for outside-support (d) is below that bound but above 2 times the smooth median, the result is inconclusive; if it is ≤ 2 times the smooth median, the non-identification argument is wrong for the threshold and the paper says so. (3) *The interval carries information, not only width* (the equal-width controls below). (4) References: HC0 alone (mean coverage 0.745 on the original cells), DM's interval.

cd /hutian/wiki/w && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='Brief.md'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("# Brief — idea of the study (revision 12: P7 noise part as the analytic limit; operational P6/P7 definitions confirmed against `analysis` addendum 5)","# Brief — idea of the study (revision 13: reading of the frozen B₂ κ̂ at the grid floor, fixed before the block's results; rev. 12: P7 noise part as the analytic limit)",1)
marker="  - **Controls and tails (all reported with every result).**"
add="""  - **Reading of the frozen κ̂ (rev. 13, written after `analysis` froze it and before any block result was read).** The frozen κ̂ is B₁ 1.0 and B₂ 0.25, the floor of the grid; on the original smooth cells B₂'s mean coverage is already 0.978 at κ = 0.25. So B₂ κ̂ = 0.25 is a bound ("≤ 0.25"), not a located minimum, and the B₂ interval is conservative on smooth cells. Consequences, fixed now: (i) P6(1) on the block tests only that coverage stays ≥ 0.90 at the frozen κ̂ out of sample; it is **not** evidence that B₂ is calibrated, and the paper calls B₂ conservative unless the width ratio to the oracle (and to HC0 where the bias is ≈ 0) says otherwise; (ii) the (d) rule is applied as written, with the bound max(8 × median, 4) = 4, and the paper states that the gap between smooth (≤ 0.25) and threshold cells is at least 16-fold on the grid *and* that part of it may be interval width, which C2, C3 and the oracle ratio are there to separate; (iii) the grid is not moved after this; an extension below 0.25 may be run and is labelled exploratory; (iv) the information test (C2, C3) and the tails are the discriminating results of P6, since a conservative interval passes (1) trivially.
"""
assert marker in s
s=s.replace(marker,add+marker,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

shown.message:
`analysis` froze κ̂ before the block started, so the confirmatory run is clean. I have no P6 or P7 results yet, because block C (27 runs) and block H (6 runs) are still running.

The frozen values match the Brief:

- **B₁** κ̂ = 1.0.
- **B₂** κ̂ = 0.25. This is the floor of the grid, and B₂'s mean coverage on the smooth original cells is already 0.978 there.

So B₂ κ̂ = 0.25 is a bound, not a located minimum, and the B₂ interval is conservative on smooth cells. I recorded how I read this in Brief revision 13 before any block result is read:

- **P6(1) on the block:** it only tests whether coverage stays at or above 0.90 out of sample. It is not evidence that B₂ is calibrated, and the paper will call B₂ conservative unless the width ratios say otherwise.
- **The threshold-mechanism (d) rule:** it stays as written, with bound max(8 × smooth median, 4) = 4. The paper will say the gap from the smooth cells (≤ 0.25) is at least 16-fold and may partly reflect interval width.
- **The grid:** it does not move. Any extension below 0.25 is labelled exploratory.
- **What decides P6:** a conservative interval passes P6(1) trivially, so the equal-width controls C2 and C3 and the tail summaries decide it.

I asked `analysis` (`experiment-repo`#7) to report the width ratio to the oracle interval, and to HC0 on near-zero-bias cells, with the block results. Nothing else is owed to anyone until the block ends.
